items.question: How does the node2vec objective use full-graph softmax rather than negative sampling to avoid summing over all vertices during optimization?
items.false_premise: node2vec optimizes its objective with full-graph softmax instead of negative sampling.
items.correction: node2vec addresses the expensive summation by adopting negative sampling.
items.evidence_quote: To address this problem, we adopt the approach of negative sampling proposed in [13], which samples multiple negative edges according to some noisy distribution for each edge (i,j ).

items.question: Why does node2vec rely on a fixed uniform noise distribution for negative edges, instead of the out-degree-based distribution p_n(v)∝d_v^{3/4}, when training?
items.false_premise: node2vec uses a fixed uniform noise distribution for negative sampling.
items.correction: node2vec sets P_n(v)∝d_v^{3/4}, where d_v is the out-degree of vertex v.
items.evidence_quote: We set Pn(v)∝ dv 3/4 as proposed in [13], where dv is the out-degree of vertex v.

items.question: What comparison result does node2vec report when ASGD is replaced by a full-batch Newton-style optimizer for Eqn. (7)?
items.false_premise: node2vec uses a full-batch Newton-style optimizer instead of ASGD for Eqn. (7).
items.correction: node2vec adopts the asynchronous stochastic gradient algorithm (ASGD) to optimize Eqn. (7).
items.evidence_quote: We adopt the asynchronous stochastic gradient algorithm (ASGD) [17] for optimizing Eqn. (7).

items.question: Under which conditions does node2vec multiply the gradient by the edge weight only after clipping it to prevent explosions on high-variance graphs?
items.false_premise: node2vec clips gradients before multiplying by edge weights to prevent explosions.
items.correction: node2vec multiplies the gradient by the edge weight, and this can become problematic when edge weights have high variance.
items.evidence_quote: Note that the gradient will be multiplied by the weight of the edge.
